cues.text: Watch F1 Finance's Audit Machine test the journal entries of HANGS Construction Services, every change made to the books.
One $48,000 entry was posted after the books were closed.
Sixty-four entries were keyed by hand, and two were posted on a weekend.
Now risk filters look for warning signs, like round amounts or entries made at night.
Sixteen entries hit two or more.
Then it checks sixteen entries, eight risky and eight at random, against their paperwork.
All sixteen agree, including a Sunday entry from the July holiday weekend.
Top-side entries are changes made by hand after the books close.
Seven of eight are supported. The $48,000 revenue entry, posted on a Saturday night, is not.
Now it adds up what it found and sets it against materiality.
Then it writes the workpapers and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

All done. One known error: $48,000 of unsupported revenue, about 14% of materiality, the size of error that matters. Small in amount, serious in kind. Ten items stay open. The CPA, a person, concludes and signs. The machine gives no opinion.
